book.echoesofantiquity.lore_book.landing: I did not come here to build.$(br)I came to find out who did.$(br2)$(o)Most of these pages are still blank. The ground gives them up slowly.$()
category.echoesofantiquity.manual.desc: What I have managed to rebuild, and how.
category.echoesofantiquity.architects.de: They measured everything. That is how I know they were afraid.
category.echoesofantiquity.fallen_humans: The ones who went through, and did not come back the same.
category.echoesofantiquity.failed_clones: Someone tried to save people. This is what was saved.
entry.echoesofantiquity.foundations.1: Every ruin I open has the same sherd pressed into its lowest course. Not decoration. A $(l)signature$().$(br2)They did not sign the towers or the halls. They signed the $(o)foundation$(). Whatever else they built, they wanted it known who had laid the first stone.
entry.echoesofantiquity.foundations.2: I have counted eleven of these now, across four sites, hundreds of blocks apart.$(br2)Identical. Not similar — identical. They had a standard, and they held to it.
entry.echoesofantiquity.foundations.3: $(o)Later note.$() I was wrong about the signature.$(br2)It is a $(l)datum mark$() — a reference height. Every one of them sits at exactly the same level, no matter the terrain above.$(br2)They were not signing their work. They were agreeing on where the world began.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_measure.1: Their tools are all the same kind of tool. Tape, level, plumb.$(br2)Nothing for hunting. Nothing for war. A civilisation whose surviving instruments are entirely about $(l)certainty$().
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_measure.2: $(o)Later note.$() The gravity anchors bother me.$(br2)You do not invent a machine to hold falling stone in the air unless something above you is coming down, and you need it to $(l)stop$() while you get out.$(br2)These are not builders' tools. They are $(o)evacuation$() tools.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_crossing.1: The strongholds all point the same way — down, and then through.$(br2)They built the frames. They did not finish them. Something made them stop, or something made them hurry.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_crossing.2: $(o)Later note.$() The metal is the proof.$(br2)You cannot smelt End Steel here. It needs the other side. Which means someone crossed, worked, and $(l)sent it back$().$(br2)For a while, the door swung both ways.
entry.echoesofantiquity.what_came_back.1: The armour is the worst of it. Every piece I recover is built around the same assumption: $(l)there will be no ground$().$(br2)Straps for falling. Weave that catches nothing. Boots that make no sound, because something out there listens.
entry.echoesofantiquity.what_came_back.2: $(o)Later note.$() I made the goggles from their pattern and I have looked one in the face.$(br2)It did not attack. It $(l)waited$().$(br2)I do not think they were stranded. I think they are still there, and still waiting, and I no longer believe I am the one doing the observing.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_archive.1: The fragments hum. Hold one long enough and you feel it settle into the same rhythm as your own pulse.$(br2)Whatever these are, they were not mined. They were $(l)taken$().
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_archive.2: $(o)Later note.$() Ten of them will wake a waystone, and a woken waystone will pull you back from dying.$(br2)Ten. That is not a fuel cost. That is an $(l)exchange rate$().$(br2)I have stopped asking where the ones I spend go.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_copies.1: The Architects did not evacuate everyone. They could not.$(br2)So they did the other thing. They kept what they could of people, and they meant to put them back.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_copies.2: $(o)Later note.$() Watch a villager long enough and it becomes unbearable.$(br2)They keep the trade. They keep the craft. They have lost the $(l)hands$() — no tools, no weapons, no building.$(br2)They are not descendants. They are what came out of the machine when it was already failing.
entry.echoesofantiquity.end_steel.1: Iron will not hold an End charge on its own. Bind it to a popped chorus fruit and a pearl and it takes, and holds.$(br2)Everything else in this manual is built on it.
entry.echoesofantiquity.waypoints.1: The anchor is the destination. Build it once, and build it somewhere you will want to return to.$(br2)The pearl is the journey, and the pearl is spent. Twenty crossings, then it is dust.
entry.echoesofantiquity.the_sieve.1: Their spoil heaps are still full. Sand, gravel, the leavings of every excavation they ever made.$(br2)Feed it a soul fragment and it will sort the ground for you, the way they did.
